Data engineering · In development

Emergency Aid: data within process limits

Chunking reduces temporary data, but retained state can still grow. I measured it before choosing the next change.

Understand the resultsCode and notebooks

The problem

Ingest data without exhausting memory.

The source is 31.6 GB. The pipeline reads in chunks, normalizes data, and uses PostgreSQL binary COPY; published tests cover controlled subsets up to 5 million rows.

The result

A useful diagnosis also shows what failed.

What worsened

With fixed 100-thousand-row chunks, post-cleanup memory rose from about 182 to 750 MiB over 5 million rows.

What the diagnosis suggests

A correlation of about 0.99 with accumulated IDs points to deduplication sets; it does not establish the sole cause.

The next decision

Move cross-chunk deduplication to PostgreSQL staging and repeat the same experiment. This correction is planned; no memory improvement from it has been published.

See protocol and interpretation →

My role

Pipeline, instrumentation, and analysis.

Python/Pandas/asyncpg ingestion, Alembic schema, per-stage instrumentation, isolated runs, and notebooks support the investigation.

An API and dashboard support query exploration. Index, chunk-size, Polars, and PySpark comparisons remain planned work.
